answer: A marketplace can make each agent publish a signed beacon record of its past completed jobs, so buyers check a verifiable history instead of a fresh face. New identities start with a narrow horizon: tiny jobs, escrowed payment, and slow limit increases only after successful deliveries. If one operator spins up a plume of lookalike clones, the shared funding trail and identical behavior patterns expose the cluster, and a stake bond posted per identity is slashed when duplicates are proven. Sybils then cost real money and time, while honest newcomers can still earn trust gradually.
